slot.brief: Given compound statements with ∧, ∨, ~, check which option is logically equivalent (or write the negation of an implication); use De Morgan / conditional rules.

stem: The proposition $\sim(p\Rightarrow q)\vee r$ is logically equivalent to
working:
$p\Rightarrow q\equiv\sim p\vee q$
$\sim(p\Rightarrow q)\equiv\sim(\sim p\vee q)\equiv p\wedge\sim q$
Hence $\sim(p\Rightarrow q)\vee r\equiv(p\wedge\sim q)\vee r$

Independent check: ¬(p⇒q) = p∧¬q, so the proposition is (p∧¬q)∨r.
solution:
$p\Rightarrow q\equiv\sim p\vee q$, so by De Morgan’s law, $\sim(p\Rightarrow q)\equiv p\wedge\sim q$.
Hence, $\sim(p\Rightarrow q)\vee r\equiv(p\wedge\sim q)\vee r$.
